Task: Add background job processing with retries and cron scheduling to a TypeScript backend.
Reference notes on some candidate tools:

### BullMQ
BullMQ is an open-source Node.js library for queues and background jobs, backed by Redis. It offers retries with backoff, delayed and repeatable (cron) jobs, rate limiting, priorities and parent/child job flows. You run the workers and the Redis instance yourself. Install with `npm i bullmq`. MIT licensed and free; an optional paid dashboard exists.

### Inngest
Inngest is a managed platform for durable background functions. You write TypeScript functions triggered by events or cron schedules; the platform handles retries, step-level state, concurrency limits, throttling and scheduling, and calls your app over HTTP, so there is no queue infrastructure to run. Install with `npm i inngest`. Free tier with usage-based paid plans; self-hosting is available.

### Trigger.dev
Trigger.dev is an open-source platform for background tasks written in TypeScript. Tasks run on its managed compute or a self-hosted instance, with retries, cron schedules, queues with concurrency control, real-time run status and no execution timeouts for long jobs. Install with `npm i @trigger.dev/sdk`. Apache 2.0 licensed; free tier with usage-based paid plans.
